findings.title: Claim lifecycle not enforced: reducer checks status membership per type, never the transition (55 of 78 triples outside spec)
findings.claim: ∃ type,from,to: reduce accepts CLAIM_STATUS_CHANGED(from→to) ∧ (from,to) ∉ T_spec; census over all 78 (type,from,to) triples: 55 accepted outside T, 0 spec-legal edges rejected; 39 leave a terminal state (RETIRED→OPEN, SUPPORTED→OPEN/TESTING, FALSIFIED→SUPPORTED, ANSWERED→OPEN), 16 are self-loops, 6 skip TESTING
findings.witness: node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/store/authority-lifecycle.test.ts  (tests 'I3: ... leaves a terminal state', '... self transitions', '... skips TESTING', 'proposal path'); minimal: fold([created, claim c FACT, status c RETIRED, status c OPEN]) succeeds
findings.observed: census checked=78 extra=55 missing=0; RETIRED claim returns to OPEN; same through PROPOSAL_ACCEPTED path
findings.fix: Add a transition table keyed by (type,from,to) in types.ts per spec section 1 and check it in assertClaimStatus; make RETIRED terminal.

findings.title: assertAuthorized is fail-open: any actor.kind other than the exact string 'ai' is treated as human
findings.claim: ∃ e: actor(e).kind ∉ {human, ai} ∧ type(e) ∈ HUMAN_ONLY_EVENTS ∧ reduce accepts e; 42 (kind × type) combinations accepted, plus CLAIM_ADDED FACT
findings.witness: reduce(state, {type:'PHASE_CHANGED', actor:{kind:'tool'}, ...}) and kinds 'AI','ai ','system','','Human' for all 8 non-bootstrap human-only events; test: authority-lifecycle.test.ts 'I2: reducer is fail-closed...' and 'unknown actor kind cannot add a FACT claim'
findings.observed: 42 human-only events accepted from non-human non-'ai' actors; actor kind 'tool' adds an unconfirmed FACT. Safe today only because zod schema runs first; reduce/fold are public via cws/core and take pre-parsed CwsEvent.
findings.fix: Invert: require actor.kind === 'human' for human-only events and for confirmed claims; throw on any kind not in {human,ai}.

findings.title: Imported/forged chain-valid logs: `at` is not monotonic, not canonical ISO, not bounded (Date.parse leniency: '1', 'Feb 30 2026', year 9999)
findings.witness: node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/store/forged-import.test.ts  (3 tests on `at`); Date.parse('1')=978303600000, Date.parse('2026-02-30T00:00:00Z') valid
findings.observed: import exit code 0 for all of them; log order lies about history (2026→2020), 'proof' of time ordering is void
findings.fix: Require /^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d\.\d{3}Z$/ and round-trip equality via toISOString; require at >= previous at; optional max skew vs now.

findings.title: I6 holds for corruption but not liveness: 8 procs x 250 appends lose 18 appends to 8 s lock timeout because every append refolds the whole log (O(n^2))
findings.claim: N=8, M=250 through real EventLog ⇒ |L| = 2000 is violated: 18 appends threw 'timed out waiting for lock' (verify(L) still ok, no corruption)
findings.witness: node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/store/concurrency.test.ts  (test 'I6: 8 processes x 250 appends')
findings.observed: per-worker failures 3,1,0,6,1,4,0,3 (total 18); chain verified; no stray files
findings.fix: Cache folded state keyed by (size, last hash) or fold incrementally from the tail under the lock; fair queue/backoff with jitter; longer timeout proportional to log size.

findings.title: fold is quadratic: 4k→16k events takes ~9x; a 256 MB import (allowed) or ordinary long-lived log becomes hours of CPU
findings.claim: time(fold(L_16k)) / time(fold(L_4k)) ≈ 9 > 4 (linear); mapClaim copies all claims per status event and find() scans; 16k events = 5.4 s, extrapolated 800k events (256 MB bound) ≈ 3.7 h per open/append/import verify
findings.witness: node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/store/forged-import.test.ts  (test 'perf/DoS: fold must be ~linear')
findings.observed: ratio fails the <6 bound; measured 2000 ev 0.32 s, 4000 0.62 s, 8000 2.1 s, 16000 5.4 s
findings.invariant: new: fold complexity bounded (availability of the single source of truth)
findings.fix: Index claims by id (Map) inside state or a persistent structure; lower MAX_EXPANDED_BYTES and cap eventCount.

findings.title: verify accepts bytes that differ from what was written: unknown keys, key order, whitespace, \u-escapes, 1.0/1e0, CRLF, blank lines; and the final newline can be mutated to space/tab/CR
findings.claim: I1 states verify fails iff any byte changed; ∃ byte-level mutations m(L) ≠ L with verifyLogText(m(L)) ok: exhaustive single-byte search (920 positions × 255 values = 234600 mutations) leaves 3 survivors (last '\n' → 0x09/0x0d/0x20); multi-byte classes: unknown top-level/payload/actor key, key reorder, whitespace, \u006f escape, seq 1.0/1e0, CRLF, blank lines, invalid UTF-8 byte in place of U+FFFD all verify
findings.location: src/domain/schema.ts:76-95 (zod strips unknown keys), src/domain/hash.ts:26-39, src/store/event-log.ts:39-52,71-76
findings.witness: node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/store/properties.test.ts  (11 'I1: ... must fail verification' tests + 'EXHAUSTIVE single-byte')
findings.observed: all 11 semantic-mutation tests fail (verify passes); 3/234600 single-byte survivors at pos=919; 10000 random mutations over random logs: 0 survivors
findings.fix: Verify the raw line bytes: hash the exact line text (or re-serialise parsed event and require byte equality with the stored line, rejecting unknown keys with z.strict()), reject CR/blank lines.

findings.title: canonicalEventString is not canonical: nested key order (payload, actor, proposal item) is hashed as given, so the hash is coupled to zod's output order
findings.claim: ∃ e,e' semantically equal with permuted payload/actor keys: canonicalEventString(e) ≠ canonicalEventString(e'); public cws/core verifyChain on unparsed events false-negatives and any non-zod verifier cannot reproduce hashes
findings.witness: node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/store/properties.test.ts  (test 'I1: canonicalEventString is canonical')
findings.fix: Canonicalise recursively (sorted keys, RFC 8785) inside canonicalEventString.

findings.title: Forged log can carry the reserved `cws-finding:` claim marker, and proposal.resultId of status/phase items can alias any entity id
findings.claim: ∃ chain-valid L with CLAIM_ADDED(ai).text = 'cws-finding:<16hex> [critical] ...' ∧ import accepts (reservation enforced only in the CLI add path); ∃ PROPOSAL_ACCEPTED.resultId = id of an unrelated decision for a status item ∧ accepted
findings.location: src/domain/reducer.ts:289-310 (acceptProposal), src/findings/types.ts:81-85 (marker only checked at CLI)
findings.witness: node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/store/forged-import.test.ts  (tests 'reserved cws-finding: ...' x2 and 'resultId ... alias')
findings.observed: import exit 0; fold accepts; findings/guidance treating marker claims as ingested findings will trust it
findings.fix: Reject the marker prefix in the reducer for every actor except an explicit ingest event; require resultId to be a fresh id only for claim/decision items and forbid/force-null for status/phase.

findings.title: Session ids unique only case-sensitively but are handoff file names: sessions 'Alpha' and 'alpha' overwrite each other's handoff on NTFS/APFS
findings.claim: ∃ sessions s1≠s2, lower(s1)=lower(s2) accepted by fold; restoreHandoffs/handoff writer maps both to one file on case-insensitive FS ⇒ one handoff silently lost
findings.witness: node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/store/forged-import.test.ts  (tests 'session ids must be unique case-insensitively' and 'two sessions whose ids differ only by case keeps both handoffs')
findings.observed: fold accepts; after import Alpha.md contains 'handoff TWO' (Windows)
findings.fix: Compare session ids with toLowerCase() in startSession and in decodeBackup.

findings.title: Auto-backup retention keyed on file-name clock: a backward clock jump deletes the backup just written; non-atomic write leaves truncated file with a valid name
findings.claim: writeAutoBackup(now) with now earlier than the newest 5 existing backups returns a path that no longer exists (pruneBackups sorts by name); a crash mid fs.writeFile leaves a truncated cws-backup-*.json.gz counted by retention, evicting a good backup on the next run
findings.witness: node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/store/backup-fs.test.ts  (tests 'backward clock jump' and 'a crash while writing an auto-backup')
findings.observed: fresh backup pruned immediately (stat ENOENT); crash leaves truncated file with valid name
findings.fix: Write to *.tmp then rename; prune by mtime or by decoded createdAt and never prune the file just written; skip files that fail decode when counting.

findings.title: mkdir-before-containment-check: with .cws as a junction, handoff restore and auto-backup create directories OUTSIDE the project before refusing
findings.claim: ∃ project with .cws → junction(outside): restoreHandoffs / writeAutoBackup throw 'must stay inside' but only after fs.mkdir(recursive) created sessions/ or backups/ in the outside directory
findings.witness: node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/store/backup-fs.test.ts  (tests 'handoff restore with .cws -> junction' and 'auto-backup with .cws -> junction')
findings.observed: outside dir contains 'sessions' / 'backups' after the call (event-log restoreLog path correctly refuses)
findings.fix: lstat/realpath the parent (.cws) and verify containment first, then mkdir with a non-recursive call.

findings.title: EventLog.open/append accept a broken hash chain: append happily extends a tampered log; integrity is advisory
findings.claim: ∃ L with verify(L) failing at seq k: EventLog.open(L) succeeds and append(e) succeeds, writing new events whose prevHash links to the stale hash
findings.witness: node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/store/crash.test.ts  (test 'open() of a log whose hash chain is broken must not hand out a writable log')
findings.observed: append resolves; only `cws status`/`verify` print a warning
findings.fix: Run checkIntegrity in appendLocked and refuse (or require an explicit override) when the chain is broken.

findings.title: Stale lock edge cases wedge all writers until manual deletion: empty lock file, dead lock + dead recovery marker
findings.claim: crash between O_EXCL create and owner write leaves empty lock ('unverifiable') that is never taken over; dead lock + dead recovery marker throws 'recovery blocked' forever
findings.witness: node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/store/concurrency.test.ts  (tests 'unparsable owner info' and 'stale recovery marker')
findings.observed: append rejects after 8 s ('timed out waiting for lock') and immediately ('recovery blocked')
findings.fix: Treat unverifiable locks older than N seconds (mtime) as stale; same for recovery markers.

findings.title: reduce is not a pure function of (state,event): hidden WeakMap id-index is stolen on success, so duplicate-event-id detection depends on call history
findings.claim: ∃ S,e: reduce(S,e) throws DUPLICATE_ID, then after an unrelated successful reduce(S,e') the same reduce(S,e) is accepted
findings.witness: node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/store/properties.test.ts  (test 'I4: reduce is a pure function')
findings.observed: first call rejected, after an unrelated reduce accepted (buildIndex omits event ids, the handed-over index has them)
findings.fix: Store event ids in ProjectState (or a Set in state) and drop the identity-keyed cache.

findings.title: Human status change or accepting an AI status proposal silently sets confirmed=true on an unconfirmed AI claim
findings.claim: applyStatus sets confirmed:true unconditionally; spec s2 lists 'confirm claim' as a separate human action; AI claim goes confirmed without CLAIM_CONFIRMED
findings.witness: node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/store/authority-lifecycle.test.ts  (test 'a status change accepted from an AI proposal must not mark ... confirmed')
findings.observed: claim.confirmed === true after PROPOSAL_ACCEPTED(status) with no CLAIM_CONFIRMED; UNCONFIRMED_AI_CLAIMS warning disappears

findings.title: Backup limits too generous: 249 KB gzip expands to 250 MB (+251 MB RSS); unbounded arrays (200k options) pass schema; rename over open file fails with EPERM on Windows
findings.claim: decodeBackup(249 KB) grows RSS by ~251 MB (MAX_EXPANDED_BYTES=256 MB, zod arrays unbounded); restoreLog rename fails EPERM when another handle has events.jsonl open
findings.witness: node --test --import tsx tests/redteam/store/backup-fs.test.ts  (tests 'expanded size just under the limit', 'restoreLog survives an open read handle') and forged-import.test.ts ('enormous amount of references/options')
findings.observed: RSS +251 MB; 200k-option decision accepted; EPERM on rename (local log untouched, loud failure)
findings.invariant: new: bounded resource use on untrusted import
findings.fix: Cap expanded size (e.g. 32 MB), eventCount and array lengths; retry rename with backoff.
